exercise.name: Dead Hang
steps: Grab a pull-up bar with both hands, shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms and a relaxed body.
Hold for the time, then step down carefully.
exercise.one_line_summary: Hanging from a pull-up bar with straight arms, overhand grip about shoulder width, body straight and relaxed, feet off the floor. One picture (a hold). Grip (forearms) is the target; lats work lightly.

setup.target: Overhand, hands about shoulder width (fists ~0.54 m apart).

movement.start: hanging straight, feet ~15 cm off the floor

muscles.emg: Finger flexors and brachioradialis carry the hang to failure (S1).
muscles.role: Holds the bar; the hang ends when the grip fails.
muscles.surface: Front and thumb side of the forearm, elbow to wrist.

muscles.emg: Latissimus is the top muscle once the pull starts from this hang (S2, S3).
muscles.role: Keeps the shoulders from hanging loose.
muscles.surface: Wide sheet down the side of the back from the armpit to the low back.

muscles.emg: Postural pairs with the brachioradialis in the hang (S1).
muscles.role: Steady the elbow and shoulder; not lit.
muscles.surface: Between and over the shoulder blades.

mistakes.why_it_matters: Not a hang; library step 2 lifts the feet.

sources.citation: Exel J, Kaufmann P, Froschauer O, Baca A, Kainz H, Mochizuki L. 2026. Upper-body neuromechanical coordination strategies during fatiguing sustained dead hangs in climbers. Eur J Sport Sci 26(6):e70197. doi:10.1002/ejsc.70197
sources.what_it_gave: Dead hang held to failure: finger flexors, brachioradialis, biceps and trapezius carry the hang; wrist movement narrows as they fatigue.

sources.citation: Youdas JW, Amundson CL, Cicero KS, et al. 2010. Surface electromyographic activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise. J Strength Cond Res 24(12):3404-3414. doi:10.1519/JSC.0b013e3181f1598c
sources.what_it_gave: Chin-up: latissimus 117-130% MVIC, biceps 78-96%, infraspinatus 71-79%, lower trapezius 45-56%; biceps and pectoralis higher in the chin-up than the pull-up; elbow range ~101 deg.

sources.citation: Snarr RL, Hallmark AV, Casey JC, Esco MR. 2017. Electromyographical comparison of a traditional, suspension device, and towel pull-up. J Hum Kinet 58:5-13. doi:10.1515/hukin-2017-0068
sources.what_it_gave: Pull-up variants at 1.5x bi-acromial grip: latissimus, biceps, posterior deltoid and middle trapezius all well above the hypertrophy threshold; towel grip lowers middle trapezius.
The steps the app shows; the pictures must match them.

clip_check.check: Both fists on the bar, bar through the fists
